newsitem.title: CHAD: French defence minister visits Chad.
newsitem.headline: French defence minister visits Chad.

text.p: French Defence Minister Charles Millon arrived in Chad on Saturday for a 48-hour visit and talks with President Idriss Deby on scaling down military cooperation between the two countries, military sources said.

French military officials in Chad said a drop in tension within the sprawling nation meant France could reduce military aid to the level it maintains with other former colonies in Africa such as Senegal, Ivory Coast and Cameroon.
"Military cooperation will continue at a reduced level taking account of the improved political and military situation in Chad," one official said.
"French military aid to Chad will always be at the top level for African countries but will come closer to the level reached today for countries such as Senegal, Ivory Coast and Cameroon."

France has around 8,000 troops stationed in Africa, some, like those in Chad, are ready to intervene under defence agreements with various former colonies as was the case during an army pay revolt in the Central African Republic in May or to protect French nationals.
A 150-member French military mission is training Chad's national army as part of efforts to integrate rival factions into the armed forces following peace deals.

Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the north, seized power in a French-backed coup in 1990. He won long-delayed presidential elections in July against southern rival and fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue. Legislative elections are planned for December 22 and February 2.
